# Recovery under missing observations

## Research Question

Can a visible-only observer recover state after a prolonged interruption?

[Observation Builder](../identity-pages/CMP-OBSERVATION-BUILDER.md) · [Temporal State](../identity-pages/CMP-TEMPORAL-STATE.md)

## Why this matters

**Observation Builder:** Observation assembly must preserve uncertainty when visible evidence disappears.

**Temporal State:** Temporal state must distinguish stale evidence from current observations.

## What the literature currently establishes

- **Source-reported finding — Adverse evidence:** Cedar recovers after short observation interruptions. ([Cedar recovery result](../../../authored/Cedar%20recovery%20result.md))
  Author-reported limitation: The fictional evaluation excludes prolonged disappearance.
- **Project inference:** Broad recovery alone does not isolate a distinction. ([Project interpretation](../../../authored/Project%20interpretation.md))
- **Project-authored synthesis / inference:** The proposed question needs one bounded observable condition. ([Observer synthesis](../../../authored/Observer%20synthesis.md))

## Research conclusion

The broad recovery question needs a narrower observable condition.

**Prior work covers:** Recovery after a fixed short interruption.

**Remaining distinction:** Prolonged missing visible evidence remains unassessed.

**Strongest uncertainty / adverse evidence:** Cedar may cover the narrowed condition upon further checking.

**Gap state:** narrowing required — reviewed inputs.
